Subject: Cross-cloud offer curation & co-sell readiness

Team —

Thanks for carving time on short notice. Attached is a first-pass SKU matrix that maps our three canonical offers to the three marketplaces: Hosted API (PAYG), Dedicated Standard (reserved/committed), Private Enterprise (transactable / license). High-level asks:

- Can we align on which offer to make transactable per cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) for initial rollouts?
- Confirm regional availability (we should prioritize the three high-volume regions per cloud, see matrix).
- Flag any co-sell or marketplace-specific blockers (e.g., transactable offer docs, partner requirements).

Attachment: CrossCloud_SKU_Matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Quick thoughts I put in the sheet: AWS target: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1; Azure target: eastus, westeurope; GCP target: us-central1, europe-west1. I treated Dedicated Standard as reserved SKUs that will be surfaced as private offers where supported.

Next step: Ben, can you validate the throughput tiers / instance family mapping? Karthik, please call out any portal/portal-mapping ops work for Azure and GCP. Marissa — once we have alignment I’ll loop in Marketplace partners (AWS/Azure rep threads) for co-sell enablement.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Subject: Re: Cross-cloud offer curation & co-sell readiness

Kim —

Reviewing the matrix quickly. A few immediate notes:

1) Throughput tiers: the Dedicated Standard mapping looks okay, but we should explicitly tie SKU tiers to instance families rather than "capacity units" — makes buyer conversations easier in AWS/Azure listings. I'll add a column with example instance families (g5, a2, etc.).

2) Regions: For GCP, add us-east4 (N. Virginia-like) as a fallback — Acme has a US-East footprint and GCP peering is relevant. For Azure, eastus2 is cheap redundancy and often requested by enterprise procurement.

3) Co-sell: AWS co-sell expects a transactable offer to be in the Marketplace or a Private Offers flow plus a Partner Centric go-to-market plan. I'll attach the AWS checklist I maintain.

Attachment: AWS_CoSell_Checklist.pdf

I think we should aim to make Hosted API PAYG transactable in all three clouds (if allowed), Dedicated Standard transactable in AWS/Azure for the initial pilots, and keep Private Enterprise as a manual procurement flow with DocuSign for on-prem.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly / Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for the sheet and context. A few clarifications from the AWS side as you think about transactable offers and co-sell readiness:

- For Marketplace transactable: Hosted API PAYG is straightforward as a SaaS transactable listing. Pricing metering & billing contract must be set up; our Marketplace team will need the usage metering spec.
- For Dedicated Standard: Private Offers are fine for reserved capacity pilots, but if you want programmatic co-sell participation you should register the SKU as an AMI-backed or SaaS offering depending on whether Dedicated is self-managed.
- Required artifacts: Security questionnaire, privacy addendum, and a billing/metering spec. If you can provide the security package (SOC2 snapshot + dataflow diagram) we can fast-track the co-sell registration.

I've attached a short checklist that highlights the fastest path to get co-sell enablement. Happy to schedule a 30-minute alignment with our listing ops lead next week.

Best,
Lisa

Appreciate the draft and input. Approving the high-level approach:

- Hosted API (PAYG): aim for transactable listing across AWS/Azure/GCP for go-to-market signal.
- Dedicated Standard: prioritize transactable+co-sell on AWS and Azure (pilot customers only). For GCP, use Private Offers initially—GCP partner transactable mechanics are still evolving.
- Private Enterprise: keep as negotiated enterprise offer (DocuSign / manual contract).

Marissa's asks:
- Karthik: produce a short ops runbook (2 pages) listing exact portal steps and owners for each cloud by EOD next Tuesday.
- Kimberly: confirm which Acme SKU mapping (we need a single canonical mapping for the sales playbook).
- Ben: start the AWS co-sell intake with Lisa and share the ticket id.

I'll escalate pricing exceptions if sellers push for region-by-region pricing. We should avoid per-region variability in the initial public listings — use a default price band and an enterprise surcharge for bespoke regions.

Thanks — Marissa

1) Offer mapping (final):

   - Dedicated Standard — transactable & co-sell on AWS/Azure for pilots; GCP via Private Offers initially.
   - Private Enterprise — negotiated enterprise contracts (DocuSign).

2) Regions (initial catalog):
   - AWS: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 (fallback: us-east-2)
   - Azure: eastus, eastus2 (redundancy), westeurope
   - GCP: us-central1, europe-west1, us-east4 (fallback)

3) Operational asks & owners:

   - Ben: open AWS co-sell intake ticket with Lisa and share ID in this thread by EOD Monday.

4) Open blockers: security artifact (SOC2 snapshot + dataflow) — security will provide tokenized link. Azure requires a transactable offer questionnaire that Marissa will share with product.
